title: Soils and the Environment
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Soils and the Environment Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Assess the importance of soil to people and the environment; describe composting and decomposition; evaluate ways to reduce soil erosion and protect soil, including Indigenous perspectives on caring for the land. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand E: Earth and Space Systems – Soils in the Environment)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on composting, decomposers, soil erosion and caring for soil. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Composting adds nutrients; plants and cover crops stop erosion.
body_html:
How to think about it

People need healthy soil to grow food and filter water.

  • Decomposers turn dead plants and food scraps into compost.
  • Wind and water can erode bare soil.
  • Cover crops, trees, windbreaks and caring for the land protect soil.
Example

What should go in a compost bin?

food scraps and leaves break down

Answer: banana peels and leaves

Example

How do plant roots help soil?

roots hold soil

Answer: they stop erosion

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plastic will break down in compost.
  • Thinking soil is unlimited.
  • Thinking erosion only happens in deserts.

faq.a: Letting decomposers break down food scraps and yard waste into rich soil.

faq.q: How can we stop soil erosion?
faq.a: Keep plants growing on the soil, plant trees and cover crops, and build windbreaks.
Soil grows our food, is a home for many living things and cleans water as it soaks into the ground.

items.q: Earthworms eat dead leaves and mix them into the soil. How do they help?
c: They help break down dead matter so nutrients return to the soil.
items.e: Earthworms and other small soil animals help decomposers by breaking dead matter into small pieces.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Bacteria break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: What does arrow 3 show?
c: Plants take in water and nutrients from the soil.
Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air.
Dead animals and animal wastes are broken down by decomposers.
items.e: Arrow 3 points from the plants to the animals.

items.q: Noah weighs the dead leaves in a compost bin every 2 weeks. How much mass did the leaves lose in 8 weeks?
items.e: 600 − 360 = 240 g. Decomposers broke down that much of the leaves.

items.q: Why do gardeners add mulch around plants?
c: to keep soil moist and protect it from erosion
items.e: Mulch covers bare soil.

items.q: Emma weighs the dead leaves in a compost bin every 2 weeks. How much mass did the leaves lose in 8 weeks?
items.e: 500 − 220 = 280 g. Decomposers broke down that much of the leaves.

items.q: Which arrow shows this: Dead plants and fallen leaves are broken down by decomposers.
items.e: Arrow 4: Dead plants and fallen leaves are broken down by decomposers.

items.q: Why should people not drive off-road vehicles on wet trails?
c: They dig up soil and cause erosion.
items.e: Ruts channel water and wash soil away.

items.q: What would happen if there were no decomposers?
c: Dead plants and animals would pile up, and soil would lose its nutrients.
items.e: Without decomposers, matter would stay locked in dead things instead of cycling back to plants.

items.q: What gas do decomposers, animals and plants give off into the air when they use food?
items.e: Living things that break down food give off carbon dioxide. Plants take it in again.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Mushrooms break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: What does arrow 1 show?
c: Plants take in water and nutrients from the soil.
Dead animals and animal wastes are broken down by decomposers.
Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air.
items.e: Arrow 1 points from the air to the plants.

items.q: Which pollutes soil?
c: oil or paint spilled on the ground
items.e: Dispose of chemicals safely.

items.q: Priya weighs the dead leaves in a compost bin every 2 weeks. How much mass did the leaves lose in 8 weeks?
items.e: 800 − 550 = 250 g. Decomposers broke down that much of the leaves.

items.q: Ava weighs the dead leaves in a compost bin every 2 weeks. Why does the mass go down?
c: The leaves are destroyed and the matter is gone.
Decomposers break the leaves down into nutrients, water and gases.
items.e: The matter is not destroyed. It goes into the soil as nutrients and into the air as carbon dioxide and water vapour.

items.q: A fallen log in a forest gets soft and crumbly over many years. Why?
c: Rain is washing all of it away at once.
The log is turning into stone.
Fungi, bacteria and insects are breaking it down.
items.e: Decomposers slowly break the wood into nutrients, water and carbon dioxide.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Fungi break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: What is a landfill?
c: a place where garbage is buried
items.e: Reducing waste saves landfill space.

items.q: What do decomposers return to the soil?
items.e: Nutrients from dead matter go back into the soil, where plant roots take them in.

items.q: What is a windbreak?
c: a row of trees that slows the wind across a field
a kind of fence that blows over
items.e: Windbreaks protect soil and crops.

items.q: Chloe makes it rain on two model hills. Which hill will lose more sand?
items.e: Bare sand has nothing to protect it, so it washes away most.

items.q: Chloe sees a problem: Water runs fast down a steep garden. What is a good solution?
c: build flat steps (terraces) into the hill
items.e: Build flat steps (terraces) into the hill: flat steps slow the water.

items.q: Maya reads: “Wind piles sand onto a beach road.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by wind.

items.q: What happens to an apple core left in a compost bin for months?
c: It grows into a tree right away.
Decomposers break it down into soil.
items.e: Decomposition recycles nutrients.

items.q: Mateo reads: “Water runs fast down a steep garden.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Hana reads: “Rain washes a dirt path into a ditch.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Liam sees a problem: Rain washes a dirt path into a ditch. What is a good solution?
c: cover the path with wood chips
items.e: Cover the path with wood chips: the chips slow the water.

items.q: Maya reads: “Rain washes soil off a garden bed.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Kai makes it rain on two model hills. Which hill will lose less sand?
items.e: Bare sand has nothing to protect it, so it washes away most.

items.q: Sofia makes it rain on two model hills. Which hill will lose more sand?
items.e: Bare sand has nothing to protect it, so it washes away most.

items.q: The problem: Floodwater may wash into a house. Arjun's plan: stack sandbags by the door. How does this help?
c: It helps because the bags block the water.
It helps because the chips slow the water.
It helps because the trees slow the wind.
It makes the place look nice.
items.e: Solutions slow wind or water.

items.q: Why should food scraps go in a green bin instead of the garbage?
c: They can be turned into compost instead of filling landfills.
items.e: Ontario cities collect green bins.

items.q: Emma reads: “Rain washes soil down a steep hill.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Lucas sees a problem: Wind piles sand onto a beach road. What is a good solution?
c: use a fan to blow harder
items.e: Build a sand fence: the fence slows the wind and traps sand.

items.q: Leah reads: “Floodwater may wash into a house.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Maya sees a problem: A river floods and washes away its banks. What is a good solution?
c: build a levee (a high bank of soil) along the river
items.e: Build a levee (a high bank of soil) along the river: it keeps the water in the river.

items.q: Which is a decomposer?
items.e: Fungi break down dead things.

items.q: Chloe makes it rain on two model hills. Which hill will lose less sand?
items.e: Bare sand has nothing to protect it, so it washes away most.

items.q: Zoe reads: “Wind blows soil off a big farm field.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by wind.

items.q: Emma sees a problem: Rain washes soil down a steep hill. What is a good solution?
c: use a fan to blow harder
items.e: Plant grass on the hill: the roots hold the soil.

items.q: Ava's school has only a little money to stop soil washing away. Choice 1: grass (costs a little money). Choice 2: a stone wall (costs a lot of money). Which is the better choice?
items.e: Grass costs less.

items.q: What is a levee?
c: a high bank that keeps a river from flooding
items.e: It holds water in.

items.q: Ethan's school has only a little money to stop soil washing away. Choice 1: a stone wall (costs a lot of money). Choice 2: a row of trees (costs a little money). Which is the better choice?
items.e: A row of trees costs less.

items.q: Why do we test more than one solution?
c: to find out which one works best
items.e: Compare solutions.

items.q: What is erosion?
c: wind or water moving soil, sand or rock to a new place
items.e: Erosion changes the shape of land.

items.q: Noah's school has only a little money to stop soil washing away. Choice 1: a stone wall (costs a lot of money). Choice 2: sandbags (costs a little money). Which is the better choice?
items.e: Sandbags costs less.

items.q: Lucas's town needs to stop erosion this week. Choice 1: a row of trees (many years to grow). Choice 2: a sand fence (ready in 1 day). Which should they pick?
items.e: A sand fence can be ready this week.

items.q: Why do people put sandbags by doors in a flood?
items.e: Sandbags stop water.

items.q: Sofia's town needs to stop erosion this week. Choice 1: a row of trees (many years to grow). Choice 2: sandbags (ready in 1 day). Which should they pick?
items.e: Sandbags can be ready this week.

items.q: How does soil help clean water?
c: Water is filtered as it soaks down through soil layers.
items.e: Soil acts like a filter.

items.q: Ethan's school has only a little money to stop soil washing away. Choice 1: a stone wall (costs a lot of money). Choice 2: grass (costs a little money). Which is the better choice?
items.e: Grass costs less.

items.q: What can slow down strong wind on a farm?
items.e: Trees block wind.

items.q: Noah's school has only a little money to stop soil washing away. Choice 1: sandbags (costs a little money). Choice 2: a stone wall (costs a lot of money). Which is the better choice?
items.e: Sandbags costs less.

items.q: Which makes compost break down faster?
c: keeping it dry and sealed in plastic
mixing it and keeping it damp and warm
items.e: Decomposers need air, water and warmth.

items.q: How do plant roots help stop erosion?
c: They hold the soil in place.
items.e: Roots grip the soil.

items.q: Why is bare soil easily eroded?
c: Nothing holds it in place against wind and rain.
items.e: Roots protect soil.

items.q: What does a sand fence do on a beach?
c: It slows the wind so sand stays.
items.e: Slower wind drops sand.

items.q: Which farm practice protects soil?
c: planting cover crops in the fall
items.e: Cover crops hold the soil.

items.q: Liam's town needs to stop erosion this week. Choice 1: a row of trees (many years to grow). Choice 2: a stone wall (ready in 1 week). Which should they pick?
items.e: A stone wall can be ready this week.

items.q: Which land will erode the most in heavy rain?
c: a hill with rocks on it
a bare hill with no plants
items.e: Nothing holds bare soil.

items.q: Soil is shaken in a jar of water and left to settle for a day. Where will the fine clay and silt end up?
c: near the top of the sediment
items.e: Heavy pieces sink first; light humus floats.

items.q: What is soil made from?
c: tiny pieces of rock mixed with humus, air, water and living things
items.e: Rocks plus organic matter.

items.q: How can you test how hard a rock is?
c: Try to scratch it with a fingernail, a coin and a steel nail.
items.e: Harder rocks are harder to scratch.

items.q: Which tool would help you see the grains in soil?
items.e: Look closely.

items.q: Is soil the same everywhere?
c: No. Soils have different rocks and amounts of humus.
Yes, all soil is the same.
items.e: Many kinds.

items.q: Which rock is made when lava from a volcano cools?
items.e: Basalt is an igneous rock.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: chocolate, glass beads, paper clips or water?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.q: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?
c: Rocks are made of one or more minerals.
items.e: Granite is a rock made of quartz, feldspar and mica.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: chocolate, metal coins, plastic bottles or tiny pieces of rock?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.q: Soil is shaken in a jar of water and left to settle for a day. What will be found at near the top of the sediment?
c: bits of humus such as dead leaves
items.e: Heavy pieces sink first; light humus floats.

items.q: What is soil made of?
c: tiny bits of rock, humus, water, air and living things
items.e: Soil is a mixture.

items.q: Soil is shaken in a jar of water and left to settle for a day. Where will the sand end up?
c: near the top of the sediment
items.e: Heavy pieces sink first; light humus floats.

items.q: What does organic matter mean?
c: material that came from living things
items.e: Leaves, roots, dead animals.

items.q: How long does it take to make a few centimetres of new soil?
items.e: Soil forms very slowly.

items.q: Which type of soil has tiny grains packed tightly together?
items.e: Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water; loam is a mixture most plants like.

items.q: Which type of soil feels sticky when wet and holds lots of water?
items.e: Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water; loam is a mixture most plants like.

items.q: Why do earthworms help soil?
c: They mix it and make tunnels that let in air and water.
items.e: Healthy soil has many living things.

items.q: Which type of soil is pale and stony and has white lumps in it?
items.e: Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water; loam is a mixture most plants like.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: metal coins, paper clips, plastic bottles or tiny pieces of rock?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.q: Which type of soil is dark, crumbly and full of humus?
items.e: Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water; loam is a mixture most plants like.

items.q: A sealed terrarium has soil, plants, worms and water. It stays healthy for months. Why?
c: The plants do not need air.
Matter cycles inside: plants, animals and decomposers reuse it.
items.e: Water, carbon dioxide and nutrients keep cycling inside the closed jar.

items.q: A herring in the ocean dies. What happens to the matter in it?
c: Decomposers break it down and return it to the soil and air.
items.e: Bacteria and fungi break down the body. The nutrients go back into the soil and carbon dioxide goes into the air, where plants can use them again.

items.q: Why are decomposers sometimes called nature's recyclers?
c: They break down dead things so the matter can be used again.
items.e: Like recycling, decomposing lets old matter become new living things.

items.q: Kai wants to stop wind from blowing a sandbox. Which is a good, cheap idea?
c: put up a small fence or cover
blow on it with a fan
items.e: Slow the wind.

items.q: A rabbit in the meadow dies. What happens to the matter in it?
c: Decomposers break it down and return it to the soil and air.
items.e: Bacteria and fungi break down the body. The nutrients go back into the soil and carbon dioxide goes into the air, where plants can use them again.

items.q: A town picks trees to block wind. What is a downside?
c: Trees take many years to grow.
items.e: Every solution has trade-offs.
